data.name: Nicodemo
data.gender_notes: Nicodemo is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In John 3:1–21, Nicodemus is a Pharisee who meets Jesus at night and asks about spiritual rebirth. The name 'Nicodemus' comes from the Greek words 'ni-kos' (victory) and 'demos' (people). It symbolizes new beginnings and spiritual transformation. The name Nicodemo carries the meaning “Rebirth, New Beginnings” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Nicodemo usually hope their child will grow to embody rebirth, new beginnings and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes spiritual rebirth, transformation, and victory over the old self.
data.etymology: Nicodemo belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rebirth, New Beginnings.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nicodemo total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

celebrity_usage: Nicodemus, a character in the New Testament of the Bible
data.cultural_impact: Nicodemus was a prominent Jewish leader in Jerusalem during Jesus' time. His appearance in the New Testament Gospels shows that despite being a religious leader, he was open to new ideas and demonstrates the ongoing quest for knowledge and understanding among different faith groups.
data.spiritual_significance: Nicodemus' encounter with Jesus represents a call to spiritual growth and renewal. He is an example of seeking knowledge and understanding beyond the confines of traditional teaching, mirroring Jesus' emphasis on being "born again" or spiritually transformed. The name Nicodemus thus carries the profound message of personal transformation and a journey towards a deeper connection with the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nicodemus: Meaning "victory of the people of God," from the Greek name "Nikodemos," derived from "Nikos" (victory) and "demos" (people). A symbol of God's grace towards those seeking truth and redemption, even in secret.

biblical_reference.note: Nicodemo appears in the Gospel of John as a Pharisee who visits Jesus at night, and engages in a conversation about spiritual rebirth.
